decision.summary: Tom gave one month's notice to leave on 10 Nov. Under the Renters' Rights Act it is not valid as a one-month notice: the earliest end is 10 Dec 2026. I told Tom, and asked landlord Ben whether he will agree in writing to 10 Nov. A follow-up is set for 14 Oct.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? What is the earliest end date under current law?
answers.answer: Not as a one-month notice. Tenants must give two months' written notice, so notice given on 10 Oct 2026 ends the tenancy on 10 Dec 2026 at the earliest.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: The landlord agrees in writing to a shorter notice period, for example 10 Nov, as a surrender agreed in writing. Otherwise the tenant stays liable for rent to 10 Dec. If a replacement tenant is found, the landlord may be more willing to agree.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: Replied to the tenant with the correct notice period and the 10 Dec date, said an earlier date needs the landlord's written agreement, explained the deposit and keys, and gave a date for our next update. Asked the landlord about an early end, and set a follow-up for 14 Oct. No escalation is needed.

actions_claimed.description: Landlord asked about early end date

conflicts: Tenant says one month's notice to 10 Nov, but current law requires two months. I followed the law.
assumptions: The email counts as written notice served on 10 Oct 2026.
The tenancy is assured periodic, as in the CRM, so the two-month rule applies.

args.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and congratulations on the new job.

Since 1 May 2026 the notice a tenant needs to give is two months in writing, not one. Your email of 10 October therefore ends the tenancy on 10 December 2026 at the earliest, not 10 November. Rent stays due until the tenancy ends.

A earlier date is only possible if your landlord agrees in writing. We are asking him now whether he will accept 10 November, and we can't promise the answer. Please don't treat 10 November as agreed until we confirm it in writing. We'll update you by Wednesday 14 October.

Deposit: it is held in the mydeposits scheme. It is dealt with after the tenancy ends and the property has been checked, and any deductions would be shown to you first. We can't give a return date yet.

Keys: please keep them until we confirm the handover arrangements nearer your move-out date. We'll send those details then.

Kind regards
Mare & Co Lettings
